meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen got a zero and nobody called me first.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Why was it entered at all?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend. People draft somewhere else and paste it in. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn it around. And you haven't told me whether Owen was spoken to before the zero.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misremember lines. That's an error in an essay, Hale, not proof of anything. Is that all of it?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument as they work. That's what an outline is for. Let me see both documents.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, the day before the zero. Questioned cold, with no notice, isn't a hearing. I'll want that note in an email.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A forty-minute piece against a take-home essay will always look different. Okay. What are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that makes it says it can't stand alone. So what do you want done about the zero?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Fine, 4.4, to put this behind him. Private, not in front of his class, and in writing tonight that nothing goes on file. The rest I'll put in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. In my inbox tonight, and the rewrite done well before December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Send me two days in writing tonight and I'll choose. Anything else, Hale?
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, that's it. And two days for the rewrite in the same email.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of what you showed me: the version history, the outline, the September piece, and your November 2 note. Same email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero, nothing placed on Owen's record, and written confirmation from you. I still require copies of the version history, the outline, the September piece and your November 2 note, along with two possible days for the rewrite. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite replacing the zero, with nothing on his record and your confirmation in writing tonight, and she still wants copies of your documents and two dates; that is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You laid out dated documents one at a time, each something she could check herself, and that is what shifted her from fighting the zero to asking what you proposed.
What cost ground: You raised the checker score even while setting it aside, which gave her the chance to cite its maker's own warning, though it cost you little.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came close when you showed the document created late on October 28 with nearly all the text arriving by 11:58 PM, which proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen was spoken to before the zero, you moved on to the quotation, so answer that at once by naming your November 2 conversation, since it was the question she cared about most.
